ecosystems.label: .NET compiler
interpretations: A compiler diagnostic is normally downstream of a missing reference, incompatible API version, or incorrect namespace.
Use the first compiler error as the primary signal because later errors may be cascading failures.
checks: Compare referenced API symbols with the pinned Truth Snapshot.
Confirm the project targets the framework version required by the installed mod toolchain.

ecosystems.label: MSBuild and dotnet publish
interpretations: Restore, reference resolution, compilation, and publish are distinct stages; identify the earliest failing target.
A publish failure can occur after compilation succeeds and should not be reported as a source-code failure.
checks: Identify the failing target and task before proposing a project-file change.
Check output and dependency paths without exposing absolute user paths.

ecosystems.label: Godot runtime
interpretations: Runtime resource or node errors are separate from managed compilation and packaging failures.
The first engine error generally has more diagnostic value than repeated follow-on stack entries.
checks: Verify the packaged resource path and case exactly match the runtime reference.
Distinguish engine startup failures from mod initialization failures.

ecosystems.label: BaseLib mod lifecycle
interpretations: A mod can compile and publish successfully but fail during discovery, initialization, or patch application.
Lifecycle ordering and API compatibility must be supported by pinned Truth Evidence.
checks: Locate the earliest mod discovery or initialization failure.
Compare lifecycle symbols and hook signatures with the selected Truth Snapshot.

priorities: Report the earliest actionable root cause before cascading symptoms.
Separate build, publish, package, game startup, and mod initialization stages.
Mark an explanation as a hypothesis when the supplied log and Truth Evidence do not prove it.
